findings.summary: The code snippet is shown before the Server Action idea is fully stated and is a lone snippet with no explanatory step.
findings.fix: State the one-line idea (e.g. 'a file-level use server makes every export an action') before the snippet, then show it.

findings.summary: Bullets pack two ideas each (what the tool is plus how it is exposed or built).
findings.evidence: Called from forms or client code; Next.js exposes a POST endpoint for it
findings.fix: Split into one bullet for who calls it and one for the exposed POST endpoint.

findings.summary: The code is shown before the idea it illustrates, and it uses an undefined signature (prev, fd) without introducing useActionState first.
findings.fix: Introduce the action signature (prev state, FormData) in a bullet before the code, and import redirect or note it.

findings.summary: The redirect point is stated twice with the same wording inside one page, and a bullet holds two ideas.
findings.evidence: Never wrap redirect() in try/catch; call it after the catch. ... Why not try/catch redirect? It throws internally; the catch swallows it
findings.fix: Keep one statement of the rule and let the Q&A hold the reason.

findings.summary: updateTag is listed beside revalidateTag with no explanation of what 'read-your-writes' means or when to pick it over revalidateTag.
findings.fix: Add one line saying updateTag expires the tag immediately, so the same request's redirect or re-render reads fresh data. revalidateTag with 'max' serves stale data while it refreshes in the background. Say to use updateTag when the user must see their own write straight away.

findings.summary: Bullet holds two ideas: the scoping argument and a separate example, and the deprecation note is mixed in with the revalidateTag definition.
findings.evidence: One-argument revalidateTag('posts') is deprecated in Next.js 16
findings.fix: Move the deprecation into its own flagged bullet or a note under the revalidateTag line.

findings.summary: updateTag is introduced without when to use it versus revalidateTag, so the three invalidation tools are not compared, and the page heading says 'Two Ways' while listing three.
findings.evidence: 1. Two Ways to Invalidate ... updateTag('posts'): read-your-writes inside a Server Action
findings.fix: Retitle to 'Three Ways to Invalidate' or add a small table comparing path, tag and updateTag.

findings.summary: Code with params is shown before the idea is stated, and a status-code bullet bundles two return forms.
findings.fix: Place the 'params is a Promise: await it' bullet before the snippet.

findings.summary: Middleware bullets mix multiple ideas (renaming, runtime, location, matcher) and the old/new naming is easy to misread; the terms 'middleware' and 'proxy' are used interchangeably across pages.
findings.evidence: Next.js 16: middleware.ts is deprecated, renamed proxy.ts ... Middleware returns NextResponse.redirect(...)
findings.fix: Use one term ('proxy, formerly middleware') consistently, and split the bullets by idea.

findings.summary: The cheat sheet uses 'Middleware' while the code and pages say proxy, and the code skeleton precedes its one-line idea for the Handler.
findings.evidence: Pre-render redirect, rewrite, header | Middleware ... Middleware returns NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/login', req.url))
findings.fix: Label it 'Proxy (middleware.ts before 16)' and keep it consistent with page 5.
